flip-camera-cut (deferral clause): the round-1 fix said to defer the --gtext-k/--gsv writes and badge/note visibility to settle, hidden behind data-tween. Not implemented. applyDerived(to) runs synchronously at flight start (StageController.tsx:187) writing destination --gtext-k and data-camclip, and no data-tween rule rests [data-city-labels] (only fabric, grid, towers). So in-crop labels still snap to destination counter-scale at t=0 with labels on: they pop small entering ch5 and a3-f1, and pop oversized (up to the full zoom ratio) at the start of the ch5-to-a3-s1 and a3-f2-to-a3-f3 pull-outs, then ride back to apparent size over the 900ms flight. The badge/note clauses are moot in shipped data (no step keeps them visible through a flight), which is why the resolved-state shot corpus cannot show this. Cheapest honest fix: rest [data-city-labels] behind data-tween like the other micro-layers, or defer the --gtext-k write to settle.

regressions.what: The round-2 move from the svg element to an inner g makes the FLIP math newly dependent on transform-box: view-box resolving transform-origin "0 0" to user point (0,0). All three frames have nonzero viewBox mins (citywide "530 -190 ...", blackBelt "1199 662 ...", hp "580 230 ..."), so any engine that positions the reference box at (min-x, min-y) instead of the user-space origin renders every flight with a large offset jump at t=0. Chrome is per-spec (shots and the suite's mid-flight probe pass); WebKit is a historic interop soft spot for transform-box on SVG, and the Safari walk that would clear it is unrecorded (see failed safari-pass).
regressions.fix: Fold one watched within-frame flight (ch6 to ch5) into the recorded Safari/iOS pass; belt-and-suspenders, make the math origin-proof: set transform-box: view-box explicitly on [data-camera] and, if the walk shows an offset, pre-compose the origin into the affine or normalize geometry.json viewBoxes to 0 0 mins in the prep script.

regressions.what: A frame cut sets data-sheetcut="on" with a 340ms removal timer, but the effect cleanup clears the timer without removing the attribute. A same-frame step arriving within 340ms of a frame cut (fast flick through a2-s1 into ch4, or ch4 out to a2-takeaway then onward) leaves data-sheetcut stuck on until the next frame cut. Visually benign today because the arrive animation has already finished and its keyframes bake in --gtilt, but it is a stale-state leak: any future rule keyed on data-sheetcut (like the existing dim+sheetcut suppressor at globals.css:1576) inherits a lying attribute.
regressions.fix: In the effect cleanup, alongside clearTimeout, also root.removeAttribute("data-sheetcut").

No instance exists in the 60-shot corpus at either width with the shipped focus boxes, so this is latent, but any new focus box, label, or odd pane aspect can surface it.
regressions.fix: Test lx - estW/2 against the left bound and lx + estW/2 against the right bound.

regressions.where: scripts/exhibit-lint-copy.mjs:180 (arrive-early resolver) vs src/lib/exhibit/ground/copy.ts:39-47 (engine carry rules)
regressions.what: The lint resolves dim as `s.stage.dim ?? false` (reset on any stage that omits it) while the engine carries dim forward through {...stage, ...step.stage}. Correct on today's data (a2-s1 and ch4 both set dim explicitly), but the gate diverges from the machine it guards: a future compliant edit that relies on dim carry will false-fail the gate, and the narrow inverse (dim set steps earlier, carried through a dim-less predecessor, then explicitly cleared ON ch4) passes the lint while the engine performs a dim cut on the memorial.
regressions.fix: Carry dim exactly like frame and cam in the lint's resolver (dim: s.stage.dim ?? stage.dim), mirroring copy.ts.
